content: Monensin is a polyether ionophore antibiotic that is naturally derived from the bacterium Streptomyces cinnamonensis. It is capable of forming pseudomacrocyclic complexes with both monovalent and divalent cations, facilitating the transport of these cations across cellular membranes. Within cells, monensin inhibits the secretion of glycoproteins. This compound is soluble in organic solvents such as chloroform, ethanol, and methanol. Monensin functions as a Na+/H+ antiporter, disrupting intracellular protein transport. It exhibits a range of biological activities, including antibiotic and antimalarial properties, among others. The antibacterial effects of monensin and its derivatives are attributed to their ability to transport monovalent and divalent metal cations across cellular and subcellular membranes.
